decisions.title: Montana pilot branch: findings that change the plan (2026-10-11)
decisions.quote: docs/DECISIONS.md:254-255: 'Station observations are hourly, so a 30-minute freshness limit fails most of Montana.' (At 1:32 pm MDT, 35 of 48 station records were older than 30 minutes.)
decisions.what_it_means_for_a_globe: Freshness limits must come from each source's measured cadence and be shown beside each value. One shared limit would hide staleness in a mixed globe (satellite minutes, radar minutes, hourly stations). Old values are shown with their age, not dropped.

decisions.title: Product name: Montana Hail Watch (2026-10-12)
decisions.quote: docs/DECISIONS.md:310-312: check Montana Hail Watch against existing products and trademarks before it goes on an installer, a release page or anything printed; HailTrace is an existing hail-mapping service sold to roofers, so stay clear of that name too.
decisions.what_it_means_for_a_globe: A globe name (scaffold D-G6: '3D storm view', 'Storm globe') is new public wording and needs the same trademark check. The site header already reads Montana Hail Watch (base.html:23).

decisions.title: A website first; the desktop app is parked (2026-10-14)
decisions.quote: docs/DECISIONS.md:315-316: 'The product is now a static website in website/, built by Python and published with GitHub Pages'. docs/DECISIONS.md:340-341: 'Snapshot, not live tiles: the radar is saved as one picture per build with NOAA's frame time'.
decisions.what_it_means_for_a_globe: The globe is another static page built by website/build.py and published with the site: no app window, no Flask route, no installer. Imagery is one snapshot per build with its source time. A time loop needs persistence the site does not have (website_pipeline.rebuild_model).

decisions.title: An interactive Montana map in the style of Apple Weather (2026-10-15)
decisions.quote: docs/DECISIONS.md:382-384: 'JavaScript (rule 4): playback, scrubbing, menus, sheets and geolocation can only happen in the browser. static/map/map.js is vanilla, documented, with no framework and no build step; Python still builds every number and frame.' docs/DECISIONS.md:380-381: 'The USGS tiles and the Folium maps are retired from the website'.
decisions.what_it_means_for_a_globe: WebGL drawing is browser-only work under the same rule: hand-written, documented, no framework, and Python builds every frame and number. The site has no tile base map to reuse, so any imagery is a new licensed input.

decisions.title: Live station readings on the Now page and the town pages (2026-10-16)
decisions.quote: docs/DECISIONS.md:464-465: 'A reading older than 75 minutes is kept and marked stale with its age, never hidden.' docs/DECISIONS.md:459-462: about 55 more NWS requests per build; the live build went from 31-38 s to 44 s.
decisions.what_it_means_for_a_globe: Old globe values (a cloud-top height, a radar column) are kept, marked stale with their age, and never hidden. D29's cost shows the build budget: globe data must fit the 15-minute build job (website.yml:38) next to the existing fetches.

website_pipeline.stages: 1 statewide NWS alerts (build.py:47-62); 2 each of the 14 towns: point, hourly, gusts, 7-day, town alerts, station readings (build.py:64-147; website/towns.json has 14 entries); 3 town-check alerts merged into the statewide list (build.py:159-179); 4 SPC reports for 3 reporting days (build.py:181-200); 5 gridded.build_gridded writes map frames into _site (build.py:202-211, 389); 6 Jinja pages (build.py:391-409); 7 data/map.json (build.py:411-413); 8 data/state.json (build.py:414-423); 9 .nojekyll (build.py:424); 10 build-result JSON printed for the run summary (build.py:425-431, 493; website.yml:107-143).
website_pipeline.output_layout_under_site: index.html, map.html, reports.html, about.html (build.py:397-405); town/<slug>.html x14 (build.py:406-409); static/ copied from website/static with leaflet/, fonts/, map/ (build.py:379); data/map.json and data/state.json (build.py:411-423); map/frames/<layer>-<UTC valid time>[-r<HRRR run hour>].png (gridded.py:40, 126-135, 984-988); .nojekyll (build.py:424).
website_pipeline.rebuild_model: _site is deleted and recreated on every build (build.py:375-379), and gridded writes only that build's frames (gridded.py:984-988). The Pages artifact is packaged from the _site of the same run (website.yml:155-159). So no frame from an earlier build is served after the next build (by construction; not run twice).
website_pipeline.asset_versions: style.css, map/map.js, map/map.css and map/basemap.json get ?v=<12 hex digits of SHA-256 of content> (build.py:361-370; base.html:12; map.html:15, 35, 192); data/map.json and the card iframe get ?v=<build minute> (map.html:24, 34; index.html:43; test_site.py:473-486).
website_pipeline.previous_state: --previous URL loads the live data/state.json (build.py:472-478; website.yml:92) and reuses its last verified alerts, point lookups and station lists when a request fails (build.py:55-62, 74, 130).
website_pipeline.measured_here: Sample build: 91 files, 2,250,976 bytes. Live build: 91 files, 3,926,457 bytes; wall time 51 s and 32 s on two runs. Scratch outputs are listed in pages_and_limits.measurement_files.

gridded.mrms: Product: CONUS/PrecipRate_00.00 only, from the noaa-mrms-pds S3 bucket (gridded.py:44-46). Each file is a gzipped whole-CONUS GRIB2 grid, downloaded whole (gridded.py:456, 679); the full grid is 24.5 million points (gridded.py:453-454). Decoded with pygrib (gridded.py:455, 464). Checks: discipline/category/number 209/6/1 (gridded.py:47, 458-459), regular lat-lon (460-461), file time within 2 min of its name (462-463). Target: 7 frames at 10-minute steps back from the newest file; a target with no file within 4 minutes is skipped (gridded.py:50-52, 533-549). Any frame that fails drops all radar frames (gridded.py:683, 690-691).
gridded.hrrr: Bucket noaa-hrrr-bdp-pds (gridded.py:48); files hrrr.YYYYMMDD/conus/hrrr.tHHz.wrf{sfc|subh}fNN.grib2 (gridded.py:554-556). Fields: PRATE surface (0,1,7), kg m-2 s-1 converted to mm/h (gridded.py:63, 66); TMP 2 m above ground (0,0,0), K converted to F (gridded.py:64, 67); GUST surface (0,2,22), m/s converted to mph (gridded.py:65, 68). One whole-grid field per request, by byte range from its .idx (gridded.py:574-585, 738-740). Valid times: 12 hourly precipitation steps plus the quarter-hour steps of the next hour (full hours skipped); temperature and gusts at the run hour plus 12 (gridded.py:594-601, 712-725). Decode: pygrib; grid must be lambert; field and valid time must match the index (gridded.py:467-478). Projection is hand-written, no pyproj, checked against pygrib latlons in tests (gridded.py:222-225; test_gridded.py:408). Run choice: newest run whose longest-lead .idx is published, up to 4 hourly tries (gridded.py:57, 604-625).
gridded.crop_and_grid: Frame box IMAGE_BOUNDS = ((43.0,-118.5),(50.5,-101.0)) south-west to north-east, shared by every frame (gridded.py:38; build.py:237). No crop at download. The crop is sampling after decode: MRMS nearest neighbour at each image pixel centre (gridded.py:156-163, 177-198); HRRR bilinear at Lambert indices (gridded.py:222-258). Frame widths 1400 px for precipitation, 700 px for temperature and gusts; heights from the Web-Mercator aspect (gridded.py:39, 149-153).
gridded.frame_format: Palette PNG: index 0 transparent, index 1 hatch, then colour levels; alpha in the tRNS chunk (gridded.py:319-327, 363-372). Levels: precipitation 48 log levels, temperature 126, gusts 76 (gridded.py:91). Gaussian smoothing sigma 1 px, NaN kept as no data (gridded.py:92, 261-279). Legend stops are built in Python and written into map.json (gridded.py:398-429, 959-981).
gridded.nodata: MRMS negative values (no coverage, -3) become NaN (gridded.py:191-198); NaN and negative precipitation are hatched, never drawn as dry or calm (gridded.py:338-360, 355-359). Radar frames carry a nodata flag (gridded.py:692-693). Off-grid HRRR pixels are NaN (gridded.py:246-258).
gridded.cadence: Every build; cron every 10 minutes (website.yml:15). Radar status is not ok when the newest file is over 30 minutes old (gridded.py:53, 699-701). The forecast is anchored to the newest radar time when that is within 30 minutes, else to the current hour (gridded.py:1002).
gridded.frames_per_build: 48 = 22 precipitation (7 radar + 15 forecast) + 13 temperature + 13 wind (gridded.py:50, 58-59, 594-601). Confirmed in the live result: map.precip 22 frames, temp 13, wind 13 (scratchpad live-build/result.json).
gridded.frame_bytes_measured: Live build, mostly clear sky, 2026-10-17 about 04 UTC: 48 files, 2,696,906 bytes; temperature mean 92,886 bytes; wind mean 111,991 bytes; precipitation total 33,497 bytes (mean 1,522); smallest 1,496 bytes; largest 116,694 bytes (a wind frame). Sample build: 48 files, 1,031,860 bytes.
gridded.downloads_measured: One live build: 198 requests, 45,673,824 bytes: noaa-hrrr-bdp-pds 34,727,683; api.weather.gov 7,300,426; noaa-mrms-pds 3,639,199; www.spc.noaa.gov 6,516 (scratchpad count/stderr.txt). DECISIONS.md:388 says about 40 MB.
gridded.failure_rules: A layer keeps its forecast frames only if every frame of that layer loaded (gridded.py:757-758). build_gridded never raises; failures become status text (gridded.py:991-994, 1005-1008). Sample frames are labelled SAMPLE (gridded.py:108-110; build.py:270-282).

sources_contracts.keys: alerts, points, hourly, gusts, daily, stations, observations, reports, radar, forecast_model, basemap (sources.py:45-138).
sources_contracts.entries: alerts: NWS alerts/active area=MT and a point check per town; each build; an alert without an outline is listed with a note; test and replaced messages are left out (sources.py:46-53). points: forecast grid lookup; last good lookup reused (54-60). hourly: degF; a wind range takes the higher number; % chance of rain or snow (61-67; parse_hourly 278-296). gusts: windGust km/h or m/s to whole mph, spread over each span; other units are an error (68-74; parse_gusts 299-320). daily: 12-hour periods paired into days (75-81; pair_days 339-358). stations: observationStations, never filtered by state, nearest three (82-90; OBS_STATIONS sources.py:33; parse_stations 426-456). observations: latest reading; degC, km/h, m/s, kt converted; MADIS flags; X and B withheld (91-101; measured 467-484; parse_observation 495-521). reports: SPC CSV, hail in hundredths of an inch, UNK wind unknown, reporting day 12:00-11:59 UTC, preliminary (102-109; parse_spc 577-608). radar: MRMS PrecipRate 0.01 degree grid, a file every 2 minutes; newest over 30 minutes is stale; negative means no coverage (110-118; timing line 115). forecast_model: HRRR PRATE, TMP and GUST on a 3 km Lambert grid; newest complete run; labelled as a model (119-129). basemap: Natural Earth 10m and Census county lines, built by tools/build_basemap.py (130-137).
sources_contracts.evidence_kinds: No kind field in CONTRACTS. Map frames carry kind radar or forecast (gridded.py:692, 754; test_site.py:503). Each source has a status with label, ok, detail and when (build.py:44-45). Words: 'radar estimate' against 'model' (map.js:1163-1169; build.py:255-313).
sources_contracts.fetch_policy: Fetcher: 20 s timeout, 3 attempts, pauses of 1.5 s and 3.0 s; 5xx and connection errors retried; HTTP 404 means 'not published' and is not retried (sources.py:619, 624-642; sleep at 628-629).
sources_contracts.boxes: MT_BOX 44.35-49.01 N, 116.06-104.03 W, with MARGIN 0.75 degrees for SPC reports (sources.py:24-25, 572-574). The map view bounds equal MT_BOX (build.py:216). The frame box is wider: 43.0-50.5 N, 118.5-101.0 W (gridded.py:38).
sources_contracts.placeholder_limits: Gust 25 mph, wind 20 mph, rain or snow 30 percent, under 40 F, over 95 F (sources.py:41). Placeholders until the company sets limits (sources.py:40; ROADMAP.md:44-45).

freshness_rules: Radar frame status not ok when the newest MRMS file is over 30 min (1800 s) old: gridded.py:53, 699-701; the same figure is in the CONTRACTS radar timing (sources.py:115).

Radar listing: no radar frames at all when the newest file is over 3 h (10800 s) old (gridded.py:54, 671-673). Radar frame match: a target takes a file within 4 min (240 s), else is skipped (gridded.py:52, 533-549).
Radar 'now' tick and ', now' words: within 10 min (600 s) of the newest frame (map.js:911, 1158).
Station reading: current when 75 min (4500 s) or less old; older readings are kept and marked stale with their age (sources.py:34, 517; index.html:78; town.html:60).

Page age on Now, Storm reports, About and town pages: build time against the viewer's clock; warning when over 25 min (1500 s) old; freshness line gets class stale (base.html:47-62, 57-59; about.html:36).
Base pages reload every 600 s by meta refresh (base.html:6). The map page has no meta refresh and does not extend base.html (map.html:1-23).
Map page age: checked every 60 s; banner 'This map is N minutes old' once over 25 min (map.js:21, 24, 167-168, 1682-1702).
Map update check: at most once per minute; reload banner if map.json's built time differs (map.js:1659-1666).
Failed picture retried after 10 s, and only on the viewer's own step (map.js:22, 1012).

Alerts: fetched in every build, about every 10 min (sources.py:50; build.py:47-62). A failed request keeps the last verified list with its time; there is no separate alert freshness threshold (build.py:55-62; sources.py:51-52).
SPC: 3 reporting days; a reporting day runs 12:00 to 11:59 UTC (build.py:181-183; sources.py:555-557); a failed file is listed as a problem (build.py:184-198).
Forecast: NWS hourly forecast updates about hourly, issue time shown (sources.py:65; town.html); no staleness threshold in code.
HRRR: newest run whose longest-lead .idx is published, up to 4 hourly tries (gridded.py:57, 604-625).
Build cadence: cron */10 (website.yml:15); concurrency group per ref with cancel-in-progress false (website.yml:31-33).
Geolocation: 12 s timeout; a cached position up to 5 min old (map.js:1776).
Browser caching: picture names must stand for one picture each; GitHub Pages may let a browser reuse a file for 10 min (gridded.py:128-131; DESIGN.md:375-377).

pages_and_limits.publish_path: Only main publishes, and only when the Pages lookup succeeds (website.yml:45-60). Pages source must be GitHub Actions (website.yml:6; README.md:38). The package step uploads _site with upload-pages-artifact@v3 (website.yml:155-159). The deploy job needs build, has a 10-minute timeout and uses deploy-pages@v4 (website.yml:161-175).
pages_and_limits.schedule_and_timeouts: Cron */10 (website.yml:15); build job timeout 15 min (website.yml:38); deploy job timeout 10 min (website.yml:165); concurrency group per ref with cancel-in-progress false (website.yml:31-33). GitHub may start scheduled runs late (README.md:85-86; DECISIONS.md:354-355).
pages_and_limits.branch_builds: Non-main builds run with --require-live and keep _site as the artifact website-preview for 7 days, with include-hidden-files so .nojekyll is kept (website.yml:93, 145-153; DECISIONS.md:503). Push runs happen only when a path in the filter changes (website.yml:18-26).
pages_and_limits.inactivity: GitHub pauses scheduled workflows after 60 days without repository activity (README.md:45-47; website.yml:10-11; DECISIONS.md:356).
pages_and_limits.external_limits: Read through WebFetch of docs.github.com GitHub Pages limits in this session (not in the repo, summary only): a published site must be no larger than 1 GB; soft bandwidth limit 100 GB per month; soft limit 10 builds per hour, which does not apply to a custom GitHub Actions workflow; no per-file limit stated; deployments time out after 10 minutes.
pages_and_limits.repo_limits_in_code: Basemap budget 450,000 bytes (tools/build_basemap.py:96; tests/test_basemap.py:37, 139-140). Fetch timeout 20 s (sources.py:619). No other size budget in code.
pages_and_limits.measured_this_session: Live build: 91 files, 3,926,457 bytes; map/frames 48 files, 2,696,906 bytes; static 824,997 bytes; basemap 384,594; map.js 114,696; map.json 47,940; state.json 45,181; index.html 18,331; map.html 10,416; one town page 18,352. Downloads per live build: 45.7 MB in 198 requests. Wall time 32-51 s (DECISIONS.md:461-462 says 44 s). Sample build: 91 files, 2,250,976 bytes.
pages_and_limits.measurement_files: Under the session scratchpad (outside the repo): live-build/ (result.json, stderr.txt, _site), count/ (count_bytes.py; stderr.txt has the COUNT line), sample-build/ (result.json, _site).
pages_and_limits.browser_cache: GitHub Pages may let a browser reuse a file for 10 minutes, so a picture name must never stand for two pictures (DESIGN.md:375-377; gridded.py:128-131). upload-artifact@v4 skips dotfiles unless include-hidden-files is set (DECISIONS.md:503).

what_the_globe_plan_must_change: 1 Re-base sections 1 and 5-7 from the desktop app to the website. The site has no app window, payload, /globe route, manifest selftest, installer or Live Storms tab. It is static pages built by website/build.py and published by website.yml (DECISIONS.md:314-321; build.py:397-409; website.yml:155-175).

2 Replace the 50 MB zipball cap and the network-off self-test (section 1 point 5; section 6 Phase 1; section 7 risk 4) with the site's own limits: build job 15 min (website.yml:38), deploy 10 min (website.yml:165; GitHub deployment timeout 10 min, external), cron every 10 min (website.yml:15), site at most 1 GB (external).
3 Replace D-G4's pinned CDN library with vendoring under website/static/, pinned to an exact version the way Leaflet 1.9.4 is (AGENTS.md:71-72; map.html:14, 191; test_site.py:459-471).

4 Replace the data-volume figures with measured ones. One live build downloads 45.7 MB in 198 requests (HRRR 34.7 MB, NWS 7.3 MB, MRMS 3.6 MB) and writes 3.9 MB; its 48 frames are 2.7 MB (measured). Section 1 point 6 ('tens of MB every 2 minutes' for the MRMS 3D mosaic) would be several times the current per-build download and cannot run in the 15-minute job unchanged.

5 Decide where heavy processing runs. D-G2's default was a separate scheduled job. Pages publishes only the _site folder from the run that built it (website.yml:155-159), and build.py deletes and rebuilds _site on each run (build.py:375-376). A second job therefore has to produce the whole site, or the globe's files must be built in the same run.

6 Add persistence before any time loop. No past frame survives a build (build.py:375-376; gridded.py:984-988). Section 3 (last 2 h loop) and Phase 4 need a mechanism: the state file carried by --previous (build.py:472-478) or a frame cache (ROADMAP.md:50-52, item 6, not built).

7 Replace D12's freshness limits in sections 3 and 4 (GOES 15 min, MRMS 10 min, alerts 10 min, imagery daily) with the site's: radar 30 min (gridded.py:53), station readings 75 min (sources.py:34), page 25 min (base.html:57; map.js:21), alerts every build (sources.py:50). Settle the 15-vs-30-minute conflict first (doc_drift item 1).

8 Use the site's words for missing data and gaps: 'No radar coverage', 'No model data', 'Outside map area' (map.js:33-39); 'This is not an all-clear.' (map.html:52-59); 'Data unavailable' only where the site already uses it (map.js:2093). Section 4's rule 'no echo is not clear' matches DESIGN.md:275-276.

9 Replace section 3's Earth imagery and terrain sources (USGS imagery under D9; W6 tile schemes) with a licensed source the site can host. USGS tiles were retired (DECISIONS.md:379-381). The site's base map is Natural Earth and Census under a 450,000-byte budget (tools/build_basemap.py:12-19, 96). Each new source goes in the About table (about.html:41-54; sources.py:45-137).
10 Replace the flat fallback 'NWS WMS base reflectivity (D7)' with the site's own MRMS PrecipRate frames, already built and checked against NOAA (gridded.py:44-47, 126-135; DECISIONS.md:373-375).

11 Remove places, territories, jobs and candidates from section 3: they are not on the website (DESIGN.md:26, 51; DECISIONS.md:322-325). Rewrite D-G3's 'saved places bounding box' as the 14 towns (towns.json) inside the site's boxes: frame box 43.0-50.5 N, 118.5-101.0 W (gridded.py:38); map view 44.35-49.01 N, 116.06-104.03 W (build.py:216).

12 Replace D-G7 and section 7 risk 3 (laptops; WebView2, WKWebView, Linux GTK) with the site's audience: phones from 288 px to desktops at 1440 px, in sunlight, over slow connections (DESIGN.md:23, 29-30). Real-phone checks are not done (ROADMAP.md:41-43; DECISIONS.md:402-404), and Chromium checks run only on branch pushes (website.yml:96-105).

13 Redo D-G5 placement. The site has four top-level pages (base.html:25-30; build.py:397-403) and a map card that is an iframe on Now and Storm reports (index.html:43-44; reports.html:20-21). A globe is a fifth page, a card, or a replacement. DESIGN.md:89-97 rejected the full-width map first on phones. Test the globe against thresholds T1-T4 and trade-offs X1-X3 (DESIGN.md:72-80).
14 Redo D-G6 naming. The product is Montana Hail Watch (D26; base.html:23). Any new name needs the trademark check D26 requires and must avoid HailTrace (DECISIONS.md:310-312).

15 Replace section 3's 'Kind (D12)' column with the site's separation. Radar and model are separate frame kinds and separate source lines (gridded.py:692-693, 754-756; map.js:1136-1169). AGENTS.md:73-76 keeps forecast, radar estimate, point report, official alert and inspection apart. Cloud-top height and other observed values need the same kind of label.

16 Carry the site's disclaimer into the globe legend or footer: 'Weather information only. It does not confirm roof damage and it is not a decision to work or to stop work' (base.html:45; DESIGN.md:167-168).

17 Re-point the tests in section 6. 'Feed contract entries in weather.CONTRACTS' becomes website/sources.py CONTRACTS (AGENTS.md:80-84; sources.py:45-137; test_site.py:350). '240 alert scenarios untouched' does not apply here, because the website workflow runs only website tests (website.yml:84). '/globe in manifest.selftest' becomes a page-uses-only-site-files test (test_site.py:459-471) plus a Chromium check like tools/smoke_map.py, which runs on branch pushes (website.yml:96-101).

18 Update the workflow's path filter and test command for any new module or test file. A change confined to research/ does not trigger the site build (website.yml:19-26), and new tests run only if they are added to the command (website.yml:84).

19 Price the JavaScript. A WebGL loader is hand-written JavaScript and needs inline documentation, no framework and a stated line budget (AGENTS.md:66-72). map.js is already 2,155 lines; moving about 330 lines to the build is an open owner decision (ROADMAP.md:60-65; DECISIONS.md:385-387). Decide D-G1 with that budget in view.

20 Generate the globe page in Python: a Jinja template in website/templates/ and data written by build.py, as map.html and data/map.json are (build.py:397-413; map.html:33-36). The browser must fetch only site files (map.js:9; test_site.py:459-471). So D-G2's tile production has to write into the site folder, and a browser that fetches NOAA tiles directly breaks rule 4 and that test.

21 Keep the text-version promise. The map has a text List and says its pictures have no text version (map.js:2065-2112; map.html:38-41; ROADMAP.md:55-59). A 3D view adds pictures, so it must list its values as text too, or repeat the same statement.

22 Replace section 3's Live, Stale and Unavailable states with the site's states: source loaded, problem, stale, and the not-all-clear wording (DESIGN.md:153-162, 330-349), plus the page-age banner (base.html:57-59).

23 Restate cadence and latency. Satellite at 5 minutes and radar at 2 minutes (sections 1 and 3) cannot appear faster than a 10-minute build. The site already says its pages can be 10-20 minutes behind NWS (DECISIONS.md:354-355). The plan must state the latency users will see.

24 Restate section 6 Phases 1 and 5. 'A /globe page in the app' becomes a static page in the site. 'Data unavailable with the network off' becomes the build's failure text and page-age warning (build.py:494-497; map.js:191-203). '30 fps on the D-G7 floor' and 'memory under 1 GB' need phone measurements (DESIGN.md:29-30).

25 Set a page-weight budget. Current HTML pages are 10-18 KB each and map.js is 115 KB (measured). Set a byte budget for the globe, measure it on a real build, and check it in the 288-1440 px width test (tools/smoke_pages.py:23).
